Marks on glass

Why glass here dries clean

Melbourne mains water is soft, so glass here dries with far less mineral spotting than it does in a hard water city. When a Greensborough window is marked anyway, it is usually telling you something.

The three usual causes

Sprinkler overspray, which leaves a ring that builds up over seasons. Run off from a wall or a sill above, carrying something down onto the glass. Or bore and tank water, which is a different chemistry entirely.

Where deposit has been baking on north facing glass for years it has etched rather than settled. Hard water and mineral stain removal.

Hard to reach

The panes nobody has cleaned

Every Greensborough house has one or two panes that nobody has cleaned since the day it was built, and they are usually the same ones.

The awkward ones

Skylights. The glass over a stairwell void. Fixed panels above a stacker door. Anything over a roof line, a deck or a pool. None of them are unreachable, they just need a pole or a different setup rather than a ladder and an arm.

They are worth pointing out when you ask for a price, because they are the panes most likely to be excluded by somebody else.

Height and safety

Why not a ladder

Ladders against glass

The combination behind most domestic window cleaning injuries. A ladder that slips on glass has nothing to catch it.

Pole work from the ground

Which is how second storey Greensborough glass is reached wherever the access allows. Nobody is on a ladder and nothing is leaning on the window.

Where a ladder is needed

It is footed properly and set against structure rather than glazing. That is the whole technique and it is why it takes longer.
